in_arabic.name: حجرا
in_arabic.long_meaning: حجرا هي اسم علم مؤنث مشتق من الفعل حجر، الذي يعني الهجرة أو Leaving مكانا، ويرتبط باسم الحجرة النبوية في المدينة المنورة، التي هي مكان هجر النبي محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، ولهذا الاسم أهمية دينية وثقافية كبيرة في الإسلام

in_urdu.name: حجرہ
in_urdu.meaning: مکہ سے ہجرت کرنے والی خاتون
in_urdu.long_meaning: حجرہ ایک عربی نام ہے جو حجرت کے معنی رکھتا ہے، جو کہ نبی کریم صلی اللہ علیہ وسلم کی حجرت کا مقام ہے، اور یہ نام مسلمانوں کے لیے بہت اہمیت کا حامل ہے کیونکہ یہ نبی کریم صلی اللہ علیہ وسلم کی ہجرت کے دور سے متعلق ہے

data.cultural_impact: The name Hajra holds significant cultural importance in Islamic tradition, as it is twice mentioned in the Quran and carries the historical significance of being the name of Prophet Hajra, the wife of Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham). She is known for her perseverance and devotion to Allah, as she is the one who carried and raised her son, Prophet Ismail, in an barren valley in Mecca, building the first household of monotheists and the foundation of the Kaaba. This story, and the concept of the Hajj (pilgrimage), demonstrates the courage, faith, and unity among Muslims, as they travel from all corners of the world to reaffirm their faith and perform this act of devotion.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Hajra also carries a profound spiritual significance as it reminds us of the journey of faith and the importance of patience and perseverance. The story of Hajra, the wife of Prophet Ibrahim, is an example of the deep faith and dedication of the early monotheists. Her journey, to build a house of worship for Allah in the desolate desert of Mecca, is a testament to her unwavering belief and her commitment to establishing a community of believers. The name Hajra is a reminder of the spiritual journey that each believer takes, as they strive to deepen their faith, connect with their Creator, and build a community of like-minded individuals. Just as Hajra built the Kaaba, the foundation of Islam, each Muslim embarks on their own spiritual journey to deepen their faith, build their character, and contribute to the collective community of believers.
